title: Company-wide policies and processes — Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendors, Travel, Templates
author: Avery Singh
body:
Overview

Purpose
This page consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard processes that apply to all employees and contractors, including: access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel policy, and internal templates. The intent is to provide a single reference that operational teams, managers, and auditors can use to understand controls, approvals, and required artifacts.

Scope
Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and vendors with access to company systems or who act on behalf of Redwood. Where specific teams maintain tighter rules (e.g., Security, Eng-SRE), those are cross-referenced.

Owner & Contacts
- Policy owner: People Ops (owner_team)
- Primary contact: Avery Singh (People Ops) — avery.singh@redwood.example.com
- Security review & escalation: Priya Patel (Security)
- Procurement & vendor questions: Jordan Kim (Finance)

1) Access and Permissions

Summary
Access to company systems is governed by least-privilege principles, role-based access control (RBAC), and periodic access reviews. Requests must follow the standard onboarding/offboarding and privileged-access workflows.

Roles & responsibilities
- People Ops: coordinate onboarding/offboarding, maintain employee lifecycle process.
- Managers: approve access requests for direct reports and validate business need.
- Owners of services (service owners): grant service-specific roles and attest quarterly.
- Security: maintain RBAC mappings, run access reviews, and investigate anomalies.

Standard access lifecycle
1. New hire / contractor provisioning
   - Manager opens an Access Request via the internal portal (request form link).
   - Required fields: name, employee id, manager, start date, systems required, justification, expected duration.
   - People Ops performs identity verification and creates account; Security applies baseline roles (SRE, Eng, Data Scientist, Sales, etc.).
2. Role changes
   - Manager submits Role Change request; service owners confirm additional privileges.
3. Offboarding
   - People Ops initiates deprovisioning on termination event; auto-revoke schedule: 24 hours for externally facing accounts, 4 hours for privileged admin accounts.

Privileged access (Sudo / Admin / KMS)
- Justification required for elevated roles. Approval path: manager -> service owner -> Security.
- Privileged access is time-bound (max 30 days) unless a standing exception is documented.
- All privileged sessions must be recorded/audited where platform support exists.

Periodic reviews and attestation
- Quarterly access review run by Security: service owners must attest to each active account and revoke unnecessary accounts within 7 days.

Emergency access exceptions
- Emergency access is approved by on-call Security or the CTO and documented in the emergency-access register. Post-facto review required within 48 hours.

2) Change Management

Policy summary
All production-impacting changes must follow the change management process. Changes are classified as: Standard (low-risk, pre-approved), Normal (requires change request and approval), Emergency (immediate remediation). The objective is to balance speed and risk for production systems.

Change categories & approvals
- Standard changes: pre-approved catalogue items (routine backups, certificate renewals). No CAB approval needed; owners must document changes.
- Normal changes: require Change Request (CR) submitted to the Change Board and approval by: service owner, change coordinator, and a representative from Security or SRE (for infra changes).
- Emergency changes: documented in the incident/EMT process; after-the-fact CR must be submitted within 24 hours.

Change Request (CR) template (required fields)
- CR ID (auto-generated)
- Title and summary
- Impact (systems/services impacted, expected downtime)
- Rollout plan and rollback plan (step-by-step)
- Test plan and validation criteria
- Approval trace (names, timestamps)
- Scheduled window and communication plan

Change Advisory Board (CAB)
- CAB members: representatives from Eng-Platform, Eng-SRE, Security, and Product.
- CAB meets tri-weekly (ad-hoc for high priority). Normal CRs should be submitted at least 72 hours before the desired window.

Emergency change workflow
1. Identify and classify the emergency.
2. On-call triage takes ownership.
3. Implement mitigation with minimal scope.
4. Notify CAB and stakeholders within 1 hour.
5. Submit CR within 24 hours and schedule post-incident review.

Backout and canary strategies
- Rollouts must include a clear rollback path. Preferred rollout strategies: blue/green, canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%), feature flags for behavior changes.

3) Data Management

Purpose
Defines how Redwood classifies, stores, and disposes of data, including retention windows, allowed processing locations, and encryption requirements.

Data classification scheme
- Public: information intended for public consumption.
- Internal: company-internal operational data (e.g., internal docs, dashboards).
- Confidential: business-sensitive information (e.g., contracts, pricing).
- Restricted: regulated or customer-protected data (PII, PHI, customer content under NDA).

Minimum controls by classification (summary table)
| Classification | Encryption at Rest | Encryption in Transit | Access Model | Retention baseline |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| Public | optional | required | open internal read | indefinite unless deprecated |
| Internal | AES-256 | TLS 1.2+ | RBAC (team-level) | 2 years |
| Confidential | AES-256 (KMS) | TLS 1.2+ | RBAC with approval | 7 years (or contractual) |
| Restricted | AES-256 (customer/KMS) | TLS 1.2+ | Least privilege; documented justification | per contract / regulatory |

Data lifecycle & retention
- Data retention schedules must be defined by data owners and map to the classification table above.
- Deletion requests (e.g., data subject requests) are handled by Legal + Security + Data team following the DSR procedure.

Sensitive data handling rules
- Never store plaintext customer secrets or credentials in source control. Use Secrets Manager or KMS.
- Production datasets with Restricted classification must be accessed via approved secure environments only; no download unless explicitly authorized.
- Logging: redact PII in logs; structured audit logs must be retained for at least 1 year for core infra events.

Data access request (DAR) process (numbered)
1. Requester submits DAR form with business justification and duration.
2. Data owner reviews and approves/denies within 72 hours.
3. If approved, Security provisions time-limited access and logs activity.
4. Access automatically expires; extensions require re-approval.

Data breach & incident requirements
- Any suspected data exposure must be reported immediately to Security (security-incident@redwood.example.com) and People Ops.
- Data breach response includes containment, forensic capture, notification plan (Legal to lead communications), and regulatory reporting as applicable.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Policy summary
Purchases on behalf of Redwood must follow the procurement workflow and expense policy. Procurement thresholds vary by category and require manager and/or Finance approval. Unauthorized purchases may be the financial responsibility of the purchaser.

Procurement workflow (high-level)
1. Requestor creates a Purchase Request (PR) in the procurement portal with estimated spend, justification, and preferred vendor.
2. Manager approves PR (up to $5k).
3. Finance approves PR (>$5k up to $50k).
4. VP-level approval required for >$50k. Contracts/legal must review any agreement requiring Redwood signatures or that contains indemnity, data-processing, or unusual termination clauses.

Expense reimbursement rules
- Employees must submit expenses within 30 days of incurrence with receipts.
- Meal and incidental limits: see table below.
- Corporate card usage: follow the Corporate Card policy; misuse may lead to revocation and repayment.

Expense limits (examples)
| Category | Per diem / limit |
| --- | ---: |
| Domestic meals | $75/day per traveler |
| International meals | $100/day per traveler |
| Hotel | Up to $300/night domestic; higher for high-cost regions with manager pre-approval |
| Ground transport | Reasonable (ride-share or rental) |

Approved vendors & purchasing agreements
- Preferred vendor list is maintained by Finance (partial sample below). Use preferred vendors where available to leverage negotiated discounts.

| Vendor | Category | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Acme Cloud Infra | Cloud compute | Approved; enterprise discount via contract #AC-2024 |
| OfficeSupplyCo | Office supplies | Use corporate account |
| TravelPartner Inc. | Travel booking | Preferred travel vendor; use portal for bookings |

Capital vs. expense spend
- Capital purchases > $25k should be flagged for capex review by Finance. Depreciation schedules and asset tagging apply.

5) Vendor Management

Overview
Vendor selection, onboarding, and offboarding processes ensure compliance with legal, security, and procurement controls. Vendor risk is assessed prior to contract execution.

Vendor lifecycle checklist (onboarding)
- Business need documented and approved.
- Vendor Risk Assessment completed (Security) — includes data access, subprocessors, SOC/ISO reports review.
- Contract signed by Legal with required SLAs and security annex.
- Finance sets up payment terms; vendor is added to the approved vendor registry.
- Technical onboarding: assign service owner and run initial security review.

Ongoing vendor monitoring
- Annual risk re-assessment for high-risk vendors.
- Performance reviews aligned to SLAs; remediation steps documented in vendor file.
- Access review: ensure vendor accounts are time-bound and audited.

Termination and offboarding
- Revoke credentials and API keys immediately upon contract end or termination for cause.
- Retrieve or certify destruction of data per contract.
- Financial close-out and final invoice reconciliation by Finance.

6) Travel Policy

Principles
Travel must balance cost-effectiveness and employee safety. Use approved vendors and follow pre-approval rules for international travel.

Pre-approval & safety
- All work travel must be pre-approved by the manager and submitted in the Travel Request system at least 7 days prior to travel.
- For international travel, include itinerary, emergency contact, and insurance details. Security will provide country-level risk guidance.

Booking & preferred vendors
- Use TravelPartner Inc. portal for bookings to ensure compliance with corporate rates.
- When immediate travel is necessary, employees may book and seek retroactive approval; these are subject to manager and Finance review.

Expense types and documentation
- Required receipts for airfare, hotel, and ground transport. Itemized receipts for meals above per-diem thresholds.
- Currency conversion: use the day-of-travel exchange rate or attach bank statement if currency conversion is applied by card.

Health & insurance
- Company-provided Business Travel Insurance covers business trips; employees must register trips that include higher-risk countries.

7) Internal Templates and Forms

Purpose
This section lists standard templates used across the processes above. Use these templates to ensure consistent approvals, audits, and record-keeping.

Key templates (links internal)
- Access Request form: /templates/access-request-form
- Data Access Request (DAR): /templates/data-access-request
- Change Request (CR) template: /templates/change-request
- Purchase Request (PR): /templates/purchase-request
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist: /templates/vendor-onboarding-checklist
- Travel Request form: /templates/travel-request-form

Template usage guidance
- Always attach the appropriate template when submitting a request. Incomplete forms will be returned and may delay approval.
- Maintain copies of signed contracts and approvals in the Company Contract Repository (/contracts).

8) Governance, Exceptions & Escalation

Exception requests
- Exceptions to policy must be requested via the Exception Request form and include: scope, duration, business justification, compensating controls, and approver (manager + specialty owner such as Security or Finance).
- Standing exceptions require senior leadership approval and quarterly re-attestation.

Escalation matrix
- 1st line: Manager
- 2nd line: Team lead / service owner
- 3rd line: People Ops / Security / Finance (as relevant)
- Executive escalation: CTO / Head of People Ops for unresolved cross-functional issues

9) Audit & Compliance

- Periodic internal audits will be performed by Security and Finance to test adherence to these policies.
- All change records, procurement records, and access attestations must be retained per retention schedules.

10) Revision history

- 2024-06-01: Document created (Avery Singh).
- 2024-10-15: Added privileged access timing and emergency change requirements (Priya Patel review).
- 2025-11-15: Updated procurement thresholds and travel per-diem (Jordan Kim).

Appendix: Quick checklists

Onboarding checklist (quick)
- [ ] People Ops welcome email sent
- [ ] Core account created (SSO)
- [ ] Baseline Slack, email, Jira access granted
- [ ] Service-specific access requested by manager

Vendor onboarding quick checklist
- [ ] Business case approved
- [ ] Risk assessment completed
- [ ] Contract signed and stored in /contracts
- [ ] Vendor added to registry and payment terms set

Change request quick checklist
- [ ] CR filled with rollback and validation plan
- [ ] Approvals captured (manager / owner / Security)
- [ ] Communication plan and monitoring in place

Contact & escalation list
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.example.com
- Security: security@redwood.example.com
- Finance / Procurement: procurement@redwood.example.com
- Incident reporting: incident@redwood.example.com

End of document
